title: The Songbook of Port Alder
premise: Cyrus Brightwater, a ghostwriter who once destroyed his own career to protect a lover's secret, is hired through an anonymous literary agency to co-write a memoir with an unnamed partner who turns out to be Marisol Vane, the rival author whose rise he secretly engineered—and whose father ruined him. As their letters deepen into love neither can afford, Cyrus must choose between exposing the corruption that keeps Marisol's publishing empire standing and preserving the lie that keeps her safe. When the agency's anonymous pairing is revealed as sabotage by her dying father, both must decide whether truth or loyalty will cost them everything. In the end, they publish the memoir under both their names, burning the empire down and building something honest from its ashes.
about_author: Isandro Thornbury is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipwrecked letters in coastal New England libraries. Their novels explore how people survive the stories told about them.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Ink
chapters.summary: Cyrus, broke and blacklisted after a scandal he refuses to explain, accepts a lucrative assignment from the Meridian Agency: co-write a memoir with a stranger via exchanged manuscripts. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: wary hope—he believes second chances belong to people with better timing, but the money forces his hand.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: The first exchanges are guarded, then electric; the stranger writes with a voice Cyrus almost recognizes. Meanwhile Marisol Vane, at her father's deathbed, agrees to the same agency deal to salvage her stalled memoir. POV alternates. Emotional beat: two lonely people finding unexpected honesty in anonymity.

chapters.title: The Voice Beneath
chapters.summary: Cyrus recognizes Marisol's cadence from editing her debut years ago—before her father bought out his publisher and buried his name. He says nothing, telling himself it changes nothing. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into complicity as he keeps writing to her anyway.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Marisol, falling for her anonymous partner's tenderness, begins smuggling real memories into the manuscript—including the night her father destroyed a young editor named Brightwater. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: intimacy built on a confession she doesn't know she's making.

chapters.title: Meridian's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Cyrus investigates the agency and finds the pairing wasn't random: someone paid to match them. The trail leads toward Alder House, the Vane family estate. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread—the romance he's building may be someone else's weapon.

chapters.title: Alder House
chapters.summary: The agency summons both writers to finalize the manuscript in person. Cyrus and Marisol meet face-to-face, each hiding recognition of the other's letters. Her father, fading fast, watches them with unsettling satisfaction. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: vertigo—love arriving wearing a stranger's face.

chapters.title: The Confession Draft
chapters.summary: Working side by side, they draft the memoir's darkest chapter: the cover-up that made the Vane empire, and the editor who took the fall. Cyrus realizes Marisol has been protecting him all along without knowing it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth tearing him in half.

chapters.title: Signature
chapters.summary: Marisol discovers Cyrus's identity in the agency's payment records—and learns her father orchestrated their pairing to control what the memoir reveals before he dies. She confronts Cyrus, who admits everything except the one secret still shielding her. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: betrayal layered over heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Last Chapter He Wrote
chapters.summary: Her father dies, leaving a final letter admitting he used them both—and naming the true architect of the old cover-up, now poised to inherit the empire. Cyrus chooses truth: he delivers the unredacted manuscript and his own testimony. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: sacrifice—risking the whole heart instead of lending pieces.

chapters.title: Two Names on the Cover
chapters.summary: The memoir publishes under both their names, toppling the corrupt heir and freeing Marisol from her father's shadow. On the Alder House porch, Cyrus asks for a second chance with better timing. POV: alternating, closing with Marisol. Emotional beat: resolution—love chosen openly, at full price, and worth it.
